Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testReflectionHierarchy` simply creates instances of `ReflectionTestFixtureA` and `ReflectionTestFixtureB` and generates their base string representations by calling `toBaseString`, which returns a string combining the class name and the object's identity hash code. This test itself does not directly interact with `ToStringStyle` internals or thread local management.

The current bug report indicates that `ToStringStyle` uses `ThreadLocal` variables internally which are created but never cleared or removed. This causes potential memory leaks in container environments such as web app servers when the class is loaded and retains references due to the `ThreadLocal` usage and absence of removal APIs. This kind of leak is known when `ThreadLocal` objects keep references to classes or data beyond their lifecycle unless explicitly removed.

From the code snippet investigation, there is no evidence that the `ToStringStyle` constructor or any other exposed method currently provides a way to clear or remove the `ThreadLocal` variable it uses internally. The code snippet request on methods related to thread local handling on `ToStringStyle` failed, indicating such methods are either absent or not well named.

The recent bug reports retrieved do not discuss this `ThreadLocal` issue directly or provide relevant fixes; they are unrelated.

Hence, the fault is that the `ToStringStyle` class creates and stores data in `ThreadLocal` fields but fails to provide an API to clear them, leading to memory leaks in long-running or reloadable container environments.

The test `testReflectionHierarchy` fails because it indirectly triggers usage of `ToStringStyle` internals (likely through `toBaseString` or related reflection-based `toString` calls not shown here). When the test runs, it highlights the leak due to the missing clean-up of these thread locals.

To fix this, methods should be added to `ToStringStyle` that explicitly clear or remove the `ThreadLocal` variables when no longer needed, and usage documentation should clarify proper cleanup to avoid leaks in container environments.

Recommended places to check and add fixes:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle` for `ThreadLocal` management methods and cleanup APIs.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
